definition: A lead agent decomposes the task and dispatches focused sub-agents (each with its own clean context and tools), then integrates their results.
details: A lead agent decomposes the task and dispatches focused sub-agents (each with its own clean context and tools), then integrates their results. The standard shape for research, coding, and analysis agents, and the basis of most "deep research" products.

explainer.lead: The orchestrator-worker pattern has a lead agent decompose a task and dispatch focused sub-agents, then integrate their results. It is the standard shape for research, coding and analysis agents and underlies most deep research products.

tiers.eli5: A manager splits a big job into pieces, gives each piece to a specialist with only what they need, then combines their work into one answer.
tiers.practitioner: Each sub-agent gets its own clean context and tools, which keeps workers focused. A pitfall is that the lead agent must correctly integrate results that arrive from separate contexts.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, a lead agent decomposes the task and dispatches focused sub-agents, each with its own clean context and tools, then integrates their results; it is the basis of most deep research products.

explainer.example: A research agent splits a question into three subtopics, sends one sub-agent per subtopic with its own tools, and merges the three findings into a single report.
